tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Chords and Accompaniment Writing

questions.question: Describe how chords and accompaniment writing are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary.
questions.correctAnswer: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their effect.

questions.question: Compare how two different pieces use chords and accompaniment writing. Explain the effect in each case.
questions.correctAnswer: A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how chords and accompaniment writing are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparative language.

questions.question: How could you use chords and accompaniment writing in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
questions.correctAnswer: A practical application showing understanding of how chords and accompaniment writing can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect.

tests.name: Extended Practice
tests.description: Self-marked extended answers on Chords and Accompaniment Writing

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Compose a chord progression and accompaniment pattern for a melody you have written. Annotate explaining your harmonic choices and how the accompaniment style serves the genre. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: use genre-appropriate chord progressions; choose accompaniment patterns that match the style; show understanding of cadences; use chord symbols correctly; annotate with precise harmonic vocabulary; demonstrate coherent harmonic direction. Mark scheme: AO3 (analyse and evaluate) + AO4 (knowledge and understanding) = total marks for listening; AO1 (perform) + AO2 (compose) for coursework components
questions.explanation: Extended answer: aim for the mark-scheme points, in order, with the command word addressed.
